text:
incident-bot: PAGE — prefix-cache surge detected in prod (service: /v1/generate/text). High error rate (5xx) + P95 latency spike across us-west-2.
alice (oncall): acked. putting bridge in #incidents-bridge. collecting traces and top keys. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre. @ben @carmen you up?
ben: on it. looking at cache metrics now. KV ops per-second spiked ~x12 for prompt-prefix store. lots of unique keys with tiny TTLs.
carmen: any recent rollouts? tokenizer or template changes?
devon: pushed tokenizer v3.1 to canary yesterday morning, 30% traffic. no full rollout but routing allowed for some dedicated pools.
james: seeing continuous-batching latency climb too. batch sizes jumped from ~64 to ~900 for several workers — looks like batching grouping boundary mismatch.
ben: hypothesis: tokenizer change produced different prefix hashing -> blasting cache with slightly different keys -> prefix cache blowup -> batch config tries to pack more sequences -> perf cliffs
alice (oncall): can we mitigate fast? customers complaining about slow responses and a couple of 503s.
ben: immediate mitigation options:
  1) throttle batching to max_batch=128 across affected pools
  2) evict newly polluted prefix cache entries and enable bulk-ttl on prefix namespace
  3) rollback tokenizer canary routing to previous stable
carmen: i'll do (1) and (3). ben — can you craft eviction command? i'll push throttle patch.
ben: evict command (run on control plane):
```
# mass-evict prompt-prefix keys older than rollout marker
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.local/cache/evict" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"namespace":"prefix:prompt:", "predicate":"starts_with('v3.1-')"}'
```
ben: quick patch for batching (applied to rolling pool):
```
# deploy: limit continuous batching window
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/worker MAX_BATCH_SIZE=128 BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20
```
devon: note: we should avoid full prefix eviction until we confirm predicate — some customer pinned keys. suggest targeted eviction by tokenizer marker.
carmen: applied batch throttle to us-west-2 workers. inject verified on two nodes. latency P95 starting to fall.
james: rolling back canary routing for tokenizer v3.1 -> previous stable. routing change staged.
incident-bot: deploybot: rollout started — 6/12 shards updated.
alice (oncall): thanks. start customer impact assessment. SLOs affected? who is owning external comms?
ben: preliminary impact: ~8 customer tenants saw >2x latency for 12-35 minutes; 3 tenants saw transient 503s (retry succeeded). estimated TPS error budget burn = 0.9% across service.
carmen: flagged top 5 customers for account reps. sending note template.
alice (oncall): handing pager to carmen for mitigation and initial RCA coordination — i'm switching to postmortem duty. oncall handoff: carmen now primary.
carmen: acknowledged. taking over bridge. continuing mitigation and validation.
james: rollback complete on all shards. tokenizer traffic reverted to stable marker.
ben: eviction job completed targeted predicate. verified no customer-pinned keys were evicted. KV operation rate down to baseline.
devon: monitoring shows batch sizes back to ~48-72 and P95 latency trending toward normal. error rate returning to baseline.
sre-bot: scheduled auto-check: health checks green across 30m window.
alice (post-ack): customer impact summary draft:
- incident start: 2026-03-15T09:10:32Z
- mitigations: batch throttle applied 09:13, tokenizer routing rollback 09:18, targeted cache eviction 09:22
- duration: ~12–40 minutes dependent on shard
- impact: 8 customers saw elevated latency, 3 customers had transient 503s, no data loss
- severity: Sev2 (partial outage for subset of customers)
carmen: suggested immediate actions:
- rollback strategy improvement: require explicit hash-compat check before tokenizer rollouts
- add gating in canary for prefix-hash diffs (track unique prefix key cardinality delta)
- add emergency runbook step: batch cap toggle and targeted eviction snippet (include predicate examples)
- create alert: sustained KV ops >4x baseline for >5m on prefix namespace
ben: long-term:
- stronger prefix-key namespacing + version embedding to avoid accidental key remix
- unit tests that compare tokenizer outputs for common prompt templates
- CI check that simulates continuous-batching grouping with new tokenizer
devon: owners:
- RCA doc: ben
- Runbook updates: carmen
- Tokenizer rollout gating: devon + eng-ml
alice (oncall): thanks team. closure plan: carmen to file incident entry and ping PMs and account reps; ben to start RCA draft; devon to add gating PR.
carmen: filing incident report now, will include timelines and commands used. adding follow-ups to backlog.
incident-bot: CLOSED — mitigation confirmed; monitoring in watch mode for 6h. please escalate if regressions seen.
alice (post-incident): great work. assign postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10:00. attendees: eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre, product. agenda: root cause, rollout gating, runbook edits. :thumbsup:
